Subject: Renewal conversation — interest in doubling reserved GPUs

Hi Logan,

We’re starting planning for our Redwood renewal (current commit: 16 reserved GPUs, 12-month term, expires March 31). The engineering team is asking about doubling to 32 reserved GPUs for Q2 traffic growth and we need firm throughput commitments for peak inference windows.

Can you share what a 16→32 upgrade during renewal would look like from a pricing and SLA standpoint? Also curious about staged rollouts (keep 16 live while adding the extra 16 as a secondary pool) and any guarantees you can provide for p95/p99 throughput and failover behavior.

Budget is constrained — we have approval for incremental spend but need clear numbers to present to finance. Looped in procurement for timing.

Thanks,
Sam Greene

Sam — thanks for the note and the context. Great to hear OrionAI is planning for Q2 growth. I’ve attached a preliminary term sheet that outlines two upgrade paths (staged vs immediate) and ballpark per-hour reserved pricing for 32 GPUs. High level:

- Staged rollout: add a secondary 16-GPU reserved pool for 90 days, validate throughput, then promote to full 32-GPU commit. Minimal downtime; traffic can be split with smart routing.
- Immediate upgrade: convert to a single 32-GPU reserved pool; lower per-hour rate but requires a full-term commitment.

For throughput guarantees we can commit to routing policies with a p95 latency guardrail and a throughput floor measured on normalized tokens/sec across the pool; we typically express guarantees as baseline throughput with a scaling SLA and a fallback path to a lower-cost, higher-latency model variant. Exact guarantees depend on your workload mix (seq lengths, batching).

I’ve copied Dev to give a short technical note on how we validate throughput and what we’d need from your side for acceptance testing. If it helps, Marissa and I can put together a 1-page summary for procurement with final numbers.

Attachments: OrionAI_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf

Best,
Logan Wright

Sam / team — following up with clearer pricing options attached (see ratecard_16to32_gpus.xlsx). Two commercial options included:

A) 12-month renewal + immediate 32-GPU conversion — blended per-hour reserved rate: $12.75/hr per GPU (annualized billing). Includes 99.5% availability SLA and a throughput warranty for baseline workloads (details in tab 'SLA & Testing').

B) 24-month renewal + immediate 32-GPU conversion — better rate: $10.90/hr per GPU. Includes reduced unit price, priority capacity during regional events, and an extended support SLA.

Appreciate it — Sam

Sam — quick technical note on acceptance testing and throughput validation so procurement/engineering know what to expect:

Acceptance testing (recommended approach):
- Joint runbook: Redwood run the controlled load test in your staging environment with your prompts/seq-length distribution. We’ll provide a test harness (k6-based) and a validation script.
- Metrics: sustained tokens/sec for 15-minute windows, p95/p99 tail latency targets, successful model output rate (no errors/timeouts).
- Success criteria: sustained throughput >= agreed baseline (tokens/sec) for 3 of 4 validation windows AND p99 latency below the agreed threshold.
- If staged rollout: we validate the secondary pool independently and run a 48-hour shadow test on production traffic routing to the secondary pool.

Operational safeguards: automatic prefix caching for stable prompts, per-request KV cache warmup, and per-route batching caps during ramp. These reduce cold-start variance and help meet p99 commitments.

Links: internal test template and validation scripts: https://internal-docs.redwood.com/runbooks/orionai-acceptance (shared view for Orion team).

If you want, we can run a short pilot on a single model to demonstrate throughput before you sign.

— Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sam — appreciate the thoughtful feedback. Below is our counterproposal that addresses procurement’s asks and your staging preference. I’ve attached an updated term sheet and included the DocuSign link for the 24-month option plus the hybrid 12-month checkpoint amendment.

Counterproposal (high level):
1) Staged-to-convert path (recommended): Start with existing 16-GPU commit + a secondary 16-GPU reserved pool for 90 days. During staging: 5% staging credit. After successful acceptance testing, convert to a single 32-GPU commit for the remainder of the chosen term.

2) Pricing (per-GPU per-hour):
   - 12-month term (immediate conversion): $12.75/hr
   - 24-month term (immediate conversion): $10.90/hr
   - Staged hybrid (90-day secondary then convert into 12-month total): blended effective rate = $11.95/hr (this blends the staging credit and short-term uplift)

3) Early-exit clause for 24-month: 12-month tech checkpoint with an exit fee equal to 3 months of committed spend at the 24-month rate if exit occurs before month 12; after month 12 the early-exit fee reduces to 1 month of committed spend.

4) Acceptance testing: as Dev outlined — joint run, acceptance metric pass for tokens/sec and p99. Redwood provides test harness and runbook.

Next steps:
- If this looks OK, procurement can review the attached term sheet and sign via DocuSign (link below).
- We’ll schedule a 60-minute technical validation call with Dev’s team during staging week 2 (if you select staged path).
